# Literal conformance fixtures — WP02

These are contract fixtures, not claimed application execution or acceptance.
All canonical payload/preimage/signature/digest/ref bytes below are literal.
They were generated independently of the future implementation and must be
recomputed by an independent reviewer. No private seed/key is published here.
Public keys/signatures are fixture material; none grants repository authority.

C/D, domain separators, raw Base64 and Git storage rules are exactly
artifact-v1.md. Hex strings have no whitespace. Decode canonical_utf8_hex to
obtain exact signed payload bytes; decode signature_preimage_hex for the exact
Ed25519 input. canonical_json is the readable same byte sequence, not a second
serialization. request_preimage_hex binds the immutable operation semantics.
The fixture Git object format is SHA-1; it does not change artifact IDs in a
SHA-256 Git repository. Git commit_body is explicit transport fixture data.

The accepted fixture set uses type-note-v1, type-list-v1, type-asset-v1,
asset-open, asset-revise-a/b, asset-resolve-ab, type-asset-v2,
asset-convert-v2, note-open, list-open and note-link-back. The separately valid
asset-resolve-mixed explicitly resolves a converted branch with the old-schema
third branch; optional-missing-target retains a diagnostic without blocking closure. The separately authored
asset-revise-c models a third concurrent branch. All other listed candidates
are explicit diagnostic/rejection fixtures and MUST NOT be quietly promoted.

## Explicit opaque object
This is the unknown-protocol payload preserved as a public quarantine blob.
Its opaque_id hashes the literal blob type, NUL and raw body; it is not a signed
artifact/record identity, inferred type or accepted head. Only explicit opaque
preservation and artifact:opaque/raw.inspect can expose these bytes.
~~~json
{
  "git_sha1": "63fa40e12a855f46a84e268cd8f78fcc85346100",
  "git_type": "blob",
  "opaque_id": "sha256:9fa8ea4783561fdfd2fc42cab242ba81343f9a8a6f60a92e1df03d9ad48c3355",
  "raw_base64": "",
  "raw_sha256": "sha256:7024097a0d311920e39f2b4ad3f336a29831ca822571c39cd199e094431eee20"
}
~~~

## Literal framing controls
Maximum length prefix is legal only with a valid full 8MiB object body; prefix
alone stalls and must time out. Partial prefix/payload and blocked response writes
use the absolute deadlines in host-v1.md; zero/oversize reject before allocation.
A cancel control does not occupy a second business-request slot.
~~~json

  "cancel_frame_hex": "0000002b7b2263616e63656c223a227231222c2270726f746f636f6c223a22686e2e657874656e73696f6e2f31227d",
~~~

## Required history and recovery results

| Selection/action | Expected contract outcome |
|---|---|
| Through asset-open only; A/B independently author their revisions, then import both actor streams | two visible heads sha256:6a89685cbd6eedd56cea2251b8d1ae50c62fe0a798778d3605964e0b5ac01828 and sha256:84aeaa769b3946345ac0e382a21a286cca290230a8b9ffc33070455ada7c5021; neither import is stale |
| Import asset-resolve-ab without third branch | one head sha256:7697c2c4fae661ac606d8c87571b8594f6e210cfb58c1bd7c53050a44a58422b; both earlier heads retained in history |
| Import asset-resolve-ab and asset-revise-c | two current heads sha256:7697c2c4fae661ac606d8c87571b8594f6e210cfb58c1bd7c53050a44a58422b and sha256:92454dfda936b7a54b362dd5e54e47cb6b00ba2b5c558bca2d312b99f91d6b0a; imported resolution stays a valid immutable fact |
| Before publishing a NEW AB-only resolution while third branch already selected | stale_revision, no signing/intent/ref effect |
| Two same-actor-branch candidates imported together | actor_stream_conflict; preserve for diagnosis, no automatic actor-chain merge or accepted promotion |
| type-asset-v2 later published | older instance revisions still validate against type-asset-v1; no automatic conversion |
| asset-convert-v2 selected | new exact schema sha256:50306035c7fea7cb3f96d104baddb1603661d5d75319db65422cbe23f5f00754, source sha256:7697c2c4fae661ac606d8c87571b8594f6e210cfb58c1bd7c53050a44a58422b, logical opening sha256:8a921099ad66ed9febf46ee495642d8cf4cb87635028e84bff279a9fd803dd59 unchanged |
| list-open and note-link-back required logical cycle | finite closure with visited IDs, preserve both records, no execution |
| missing-exact-type / missing-required-target | incomplete_dependency; opaque preservation possible, accepted promotion refused |
| unsupported-schema | unsupported_schema; signature integrity can be inspected, semantic validity/promotion not attested |
| unknown-protocol | opaque_unverified only; no native chain relaxation or accepted promotion |
| actor-key-mismatch / signature-tamper / signed noncanonical controls | verification_failure/invalid_input before accepted promotion |
| Exact type/open replay after later heads or changed current state | original signed identity; no append; current observation fields may be fresh |
| Changed content/schema/parents under existing actor/key | operation_conflict before current-head comparison; diagnostic signed candidates are never emitted by the host |

For a pre-publication interruption, retain the exact immutable actor/key/request
descriptor and observed expected-old ref. Lookup is uncertain while the durable
attempt remains unresolved; a verified complete absence plus proven stopped writer
can later establish verified_absent. For a post-publication/pre-ack interruption,
the same fixture's public actor/key/request returns found and its original event ID,
even if the private result record was never written. Missing private intent alone
does not negate a public found operation. Changed replay never creates a fresh key.
Live implementation tests must interrupt on BOTH sides of the real update-ref
boundary and inspect journal, signed object/ref and process state. These are expected
recovery states, not claims that WP02 executed future publication machinery.

## Real native visibility fixture and public closure

The following underlying native observations are ACTUAL: the unchanged frozen
WP01 standard binary selected explicit native contribution policy, created one
issue and performed hide/restore without editing its native signed history.
The public issue/submission/receipt/decision bytes below and every signature were
verified; their public Git closure reconstructs without private files. The native
policy is an explicit fixture trust selection, not an extension-provided authority.
This does not qualify the future host. First extraction-only setup failed because
the generator looked for .json instead of the actual .payload files; its script and
repository remain external. Corrected generation retained a per-command transcript
and completed. No failure was relabeled as an application pass.

## Literal observation/cut/removal examples

The next objects are calculated EXPECTED host frames from those real native
visibility states, not observed future-host output. Tokens beginning "fixture-"
stand for opaque host-issued fixture tokens and are not production authentication
tokens. The deterministic source/view/snapshot digests use the exact descriptors
shown; repository_id uses the literal conceptual local path /fixture/repo/.git.
The actual temporary repository path is not exported as portable project identity.

A client first commits visible, then hidden (empty complete replacement removes
the previously exported resource), then restored. The issue/revision ID is
unchanged throughout. Calling since across an unverifiable changed moderation view
returns checkpoint_invalidated/rescan_required, after which an explicit capture
produces the shown new complete replacement. Do not pretend an old cursor remains
valid across those cuts.

For interrupted multi-page replacement, take any valid two-entry selection:
page 1 has complete=false,next_cursor set,checkpoint=null; the client stages
entries but keeps its previous committed visible set/checkpoint. An interruption,
expiry, host restart or authority/selection change discards that staging.
Only the verified final page complete=true,next_cursor=null may atomically replace
the complete exact selection AND advance its checkpoint. Duplicate pages dedupe
by repository/selection/resource/revisions. A page-size change never repairs a
10001-entry capture. These are mandatory live cases, not a timestamp event log.

## Exact frame-byte boundary

Whitespace is legal in transport JSON, although signed artifact JSON is canonical.
These recipes specify every byte for the large frame pair without embedding
another 16MiB of spaces. Literal smaller signed payloads/preimages above are not
replaced by these size recipes. The over-limit prefix refuses before its body is
allocated; the at-limit complete body proceeds to ordinary grant/method validation.

~~~json
[
  {
    "base_request_utf8": "{\"method\":\"capabilities.list\",\"params\":{},\"protocol\":\"hn.extension/1\",\"request_id\":\"r1\"}",
    "expected": "accept framing, dispatch normal request",
    "payload_bytes": 8388608,
    "payload_sha256": "sha256:47e696d9f9f9a049c2a8b3cb400f5778b0063ed1724ebb103a67d139cb6a4b30",
    "prefix_hex": "00800000",
    "recipe": "literal capabilities request JSON followed by ASCII spaces to payload_bytes"
  },
  {
    "base_request_utf8": "{\"method\":\"capabilities.list\",\"params\":{},\"protocol\":\"hn.extension/1\",\"request_id\":\"r1\"}",
    "expected": "resource_limit before payload allocation",
    "payload_bytes": 8388609,
    "payload_sha256": "sha256:765923df20ec6a4ca3a4700906a83ea8327ed4d61f08f40898a0b9bdcf70088a",
    "prefix_hex": "00800001",
    "recipe": "literal capabilities request JSON followed by ASCII spaces to payload_bytes"
  }
]
~~~

## Complete bounded-consumer and semantic control matrix

Each row specifies a positive fixture and its violating partner, expected stage
and effect assertion. Size/count equality is permitted by that particular bounded
consumer, but all OTHER semantic constraints still apply. A dominated ceiling
(e.g. 128KiB type payload when its schema is <=64KiB and its other fields are small)
does not imply a semantically valid object can fill that ceiling: test the bounded
consumer at equality AND the valid signed positive examples above. Never label an
input semantically valid merely because its byte counter accepted it.

For all rows, generation is deterministic: start from the named literal
type/open/frame above, retain all unrelated fields, substitute the described count
or byte content, recompute its request and (for fixture-only signed candidates)
signature with the fixture actor. Large byte padding is ASCII x; distinct strings
are p0,p1,...; IDs are D(UTF8("boundary:"+decimal index)) where actual history is
not required by the bounded component. A missing-history fixture is never claimed
as a successful public promotion. Live mutation/import pairs supply real verified
closure and assert no journal/sign/ref publication on refusal.

| Bound / component | Positive fixture | Violating partner | Expected refusal/stage |
|---|---|---|---|
| private custom intent2MiB |bounded private intent byte consumer2097152; normal exact request is valid positive |2097153 |resource_limit before publication, uncertain_operation after; never delete pending evidence |
| envelope 1048576 bytes | asset-open with content x-padding to exact C-envelope length, recomputed fixed-size digests | one extra x | resource_limit before signing/publication |
| type 131072 bytes | bounded type-byte consumer exactly ceiling; normal type-asset-v1 is semantic positive | 131073 bytes | resource_limit before parsing/signing; smaller schema ceiling still applies |
| included schema 65536 bytes | valid string enum with one x-string padded to exact schema C size | one extra x | resource_limit before schema evaluation |
| schema/value modeled depth 8 | object field with seven nested arrays and scalar leaf, each maxItems=1, matching value | eighth nested array (depth9) | resource_limit, no recursion beyond bound |
| object properties 64 | schema with distinct p0..p63 integer properties and matching fields | p64 added | resource_limit before sign |
| array/list/parent/enum 1024 | 1024 integers; 1024 unique members; verified 1024-head resolution; 1024 distinct enum strings respectively | 1025 | resource_limit; a synthetic parent list alone is NOT valid history |
| relationships 256 | distinct relation names with one known target | 257 | resource_limit before closure publication |
| title 1024 bytes | nonblank x repeated1024 | 1025 | invalid_input before sign |
| operation128 / member ID128 | x128 | x129 | invalid_input before intent/sign |
| namespace/name/field-name64 | a followed by63 x | a followed by64 x | invalid_input |
| schema_version2147483647 | valid type version with that integer | 2147483648 | invalid_input |
| sequence9007199254740991 | bounded scalar reader equality with valid-prefix contract | 9007199254740992 | invalid_input; a lone huge sequence never passes chain verification |
| scalar integer domain | -9007199254740991,0,9007199254740991 | fraction/exponent/-0/one beyond range | invalid_input before canonical/sign |
| exact key grammar | published actor/key/ref bytes above | uppercase digest, padded raw Base64, wrong actor, noncanonical JSON, duplicate key | invalid_input/verification_failure; no promotion |
| schema language/keywords | type-asset-v1 | hn.schema/9, remote reference, unknown keyword, recursive reference, executable validator | unsupported_schema/invalid_input, no execution |
| schema string maxBytes | exact declared byte cap (multibyte UTF-8 counts bytes) | one byte over | invalid_input |
| schema array maxItems | exact declared item cap | one item over | invalid_input/resource_limit at global cap |
| integer min/max/enum | inclusive endpoint / enumerated value | outside interval / absent enum member | invalid_input |
| required/unknown fields | all required properties and no extras | omit required/add unknown/duplicate required | invalid_input |
| schema collections | distinct nonempty enum and required names in properties | empty/duplicate enum, unknown required name, additionalProperties=true | invalid_input |
| ordered members | same members with explicit retained IDs/order | duplicate member_id / malformed target mode | invalid_input; no implicit reorder |
| links/closure | required logical cycle with visited set, optional missing target | missing required exact target/type, wrong logical opening, unsupported schema | incomplete_dependency/unsupported_schema; no accepted promotion |
| exchange wire16MiB | bounded consumer16777216 |16777217 | resource_limit while reading |
| exchange decoded32MiB | decoded aggregate33554432 |33554433 | resource_limit before unbounded spool |
| exchange objects4096 / records2048 | distinct exact verified object/record closure at cap |4097 /2049 | resource_limit, no partial accepted-ref transaction |
| exchange ancestry256 | complete valid chain depth256 |257 | resource_limit, no partial promotion |
| validation/copy stage30s | completes before parent deadline |blocked beyond30s | cancelled before effect, uncertain if dispatched; synchronous caveat explicit |
| read/catalog refs/records100000 | bounded complete selected index at cap |100001 | resource_limit; no silent partial catalog |
| Git object8MiB / aggregate256MiB |8388608 /268435456 |one extra byte | resource_limit while consuming |
| regex pattern4096 | valid nonexpanding ASCII pattern of4096 UTF-8 bytes |4097 | resource_limit before matching |
| regex expanded/compiled instructions4096 | exact estimated/compiled instruction counter equality |4097 | resource_limit before output |
| regex estimated selection work64Mi |67108864 instruction-bytes over COMPLETE selection |67108865 | resource_limit before first result, no truncation |
| frame8MiB | exact padded request pair above |oversize/zero prefix, invalid Unicode/duplicate envelope | resource_limit/invalid_input before allocation/dispatch |
| manifest/declaration128KiB | valid manifest plus legal transport whitespace at131072 |131073 | resource_limit before any executable probe |
| registry/enablement1MiB | bounded valid registry + legal whitespace1048576 |1048577 | resource_limit, no implicit repair |
| registry/enablement128 entries |128 distinct modules |129 | resource_limit before state replacement |
| argv64 /4096each /65536aggregate |exact count and UTF-8 bytes, no NUL |one over or NUL | resource_limit/invalid_input before spawn |
| executable128MiB |regular executable byte consumer134217728 |134217729 | resource_limit during hashing, no spawn |
| grants256 / actions7 |256 valid grants / all7 distinct permitted actions |257 / eighth or duplicate action | resource_limit/invalid_input; no widened grant |
| method inventory14 |all14 declared method names once |unknown name or duplicate | invalid_input; no unsupported dispatch |
| request ID128 / module version64 |printable non-whitespace ASCII at cap |one over, control or whitespace | invalid_input before intent |
| error/token4096 bytes |sanitized text/valid token at byte cap |4097 | resource_limit; never secret-bearing truncation |
| startup10s |full ready frame before deadline |three prefix bytes then stall, partial payload, blocked hello | cancelled/unavailable before business dispatch |
| idle/read30s |valid frame/response before deadline |no prefix, partial frame, blocked response beyond deadline | cancelled, no indefinite wait |
| mutation240s/max240s |writer completes under parent/native deadline |timeout_ms240001 or expired write | invalid_input for too-large request; uncertain after dispatch |
| request timeout lower bound |timeout_ms=1 |0 or negative | invalid_input before dispatch |
| stderr64KiB |65536 bytes |65537 | resource_limit + owned child cleanup, no public stderr leak |
| business outstanding1 |one request plus matching cancel control |second business / cancel wrong ID | invalid_input, session closes, dispatched write uncertain |
| sessions4 |four separate owned sessions same physical repo |fifth | resource_limit; no contribution lock held while idle |
| TERM/KILL2s / exit5s |cooperative exit then TERM-ignoring child killed by2s |owned child persists beyond5s | observed cleanup failure, never false successful disable |
| revocation observation250ms |epoch change noticed within bound |ignored epoch or stale-session grant reused | qualification failure/denied_access before next dispatch |
| page1..200 |1 and200, empty final selection allowed |0 /201 | invalid_input/resource_limit; no omitted full state |
| capture10000 /16MiB |complete set at10000/16777216 |10001/16777217 | resource_limit before capture completion; smaller page cannot fix it |
| capture10min |same cut and valid page before expiry |expired/restarted/missing capture or changed view/selection | checkpoint_invalidated/rescan_required |
| single opaque full response |complete raw object+Base64/JSON fits8MiB |legal8MiB raw object expands past frame | resource_limit; explicit CLI/file diagnostic export, not smaller-page fiction |
| safe public/private boundary |known accepted/opaque public fixture selections |arbitrary ODB/file/private journal/signing root via opaque ID | denied_access/not_found; no file/credential leakage |

These fixture specifications define expected behavior for later live entry-point
tests. WP02 has executed only independent cryptographic/data checks and the
small existing-native visibility fixture; it has NOT executed future artifact,
host, exchange, regex, deadline or default-failure-matrix implementations.

## Literal publication/lookup state fixtures

These are complete constructed PRIVATE-FORMAT EXAMPLES using already public
fixture data and conceptual repository identity, not copied actual private files
or an export entitlement. They must never be included by selected public export.
The pre/post source cuts use literal Git commits from the signed vectors above.

A crash with prepared/publishing state retains uncertainty. Complete absence
without that pending evidence can be verified absent after writer settlement.
Post-update-ref public history proves found even if publishing state never became
published or its acknowledgement was lost. This explicitly separates all three
outcomes; a producer must not manufacture absence from a missing descriptor.
The live implementation must exercise these transitions through its real writer;
WP02's table and exact bytes are not an execution pass.
